473: Theorem 4.4 .
474: For any valid \varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N), the equations
475: (13)
476: \left\{\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu)=d_{\nu}\mid\nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}\right\}
477: are inconsistent whenever d_{\nu}=0 for all wide \nu, and d_{\rho}\neq 0 for some tall \rho.
478: Proof.
479: Suppose first that
480: N\leq\min(j,n-r-i).
481: By Lemma 4.2 , we have \operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\rho)\in W.
482: The restriction d_{\nu}=0 when \nu is wide would then force d_{\rho}=0, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus the equations ( 13 ) are inconsistent.
483: Now suppose that
484: N>\min(j,n-r-i).
485: Choose q so that N\leq\min(2^{q}j,4^{q}n-2^{q}r-i). Let
486: \widehat{\varphi}=(\widehat{n},\widehat{r},i,\widehat{j},a,b,N),\quad\mbox{where}\quad\widehat{n}=4^{q}n,\quad\widehat{r}=2^{q}r,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\widehat{j}=2^{q}j.
487: For each \nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}, let \widehat{\nu}\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat{\varphi}} be the partition with \widehat{\nu}_{B}=\nu_{B} and \widehat{\nu}_{R}=\nu_{R}. For \tau\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat{\varphi}}, define
488: e_{\tau}=\begin{cases}d_{\nu}&\mbox{ if }\tau=\widehat{\nu}\mbox{ for some }\nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi},\\
489: 0&\mbox{ otherwise.}\end{cases}
490: By the previous argument, the equations
491: (14)
492: \left\{\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat{\varphi}}(\tau)=e_{\tau}\mid\tau\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat{\varphi}}\right\}
493: are inconsistent. By Lemma 4.3 , the equations ( 13 ) can be obtained by setting certain variables to zero in ( 14 ). Setting variables to zero in an inconsistent linear system produces the same.
494: ∎
